title: Segmented economic telemetry assembler for per-route & model attribution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a resilient backend assembler that ingests segmented telemetry (ingestion logs, runtime token ledgers, batching traces, and KV cache metrics) and produces deterministic per-route, per-model, and per-customer cost and latency breakdowns. The service must work for both streaming (chat/streaming generation) and batch inference, handle late-arriving events, and provide reconciliation hooks that align with the billing ledger. Goals: 1) a single canonical attribution output used by Console dashboards and chargeback exports; 2) explainable decomposition traces for why units were charged to a route/model/customer; 3) operational SLAs for processing latency and reconciliation windows.
acceptance_criteria: Assembler consumes telemetry from kafka-topics: tokens-ledger-v2, runtime-traces, batching-events, cache-metrics and reconciles into per-route-model-customer rows within the configured window (default 2h)
Unit tests and integration tests validate attribution for streaming sessions with prefix caching and for batched requests that split across multiple kernels
End-to-end latency for 95th percentile pipeline processing <= 5 minutes for typical daily shards (50M events)
Reconciliation job surfaces mismatches > 0.1% vs billing-ledger and produces actionable alerts in PagerDuty/Slack playbook
Output schema documented and consumed by Console chargeback UI and nightly CSV export; migration guide included
Backfill tool can re-assemble a 7-day sliding window to repair late-arriving events without double-counting charge units
description_notes: Design trade-offs: we considered two designs — (A) strong eager enrichment at ingestion time (more CPU, simpler downstream joins) vs (B) late-binding assembly using sharded joins (lower ingestion cost, more complex job). We selected (B) with a small eager enrichment layer to tag high-cardinality fields (route_id, model_variant) at the producer to reduce shuffle. This reduces cost on the ingestion cluster and keeps the assembler stateless enough for rolling upgrades.
updates: 2026-01-20: Kickoff meeting. Agreed on required telemetry topics and initial schema. Action: ENG infra to expose tokens-ledger-v2 with consistent partition key (customer_id-route_id).

2026-01-28: Prototype assembler that joins tokens-ledger-v2 and batching-events. Found 3% discrepancy due to missing session_id in older runtime traces. Added session stitching heuristic and retry logic for traces without session_id.

2026-02-05: Performance test (50M synthetic events) shows memory hotspot during large-session joins. Decided to add an intermediate sharded spill-to-disk step and limit in-memory state to 50k sessions per shard. Trade-off documented in design doc.
2026-02-12: Security review requested for telemetry retention. CIDR and S3 encryption checks completed. KMS integration deferred to post-MVP (ticket ENG-79310).

2026-02-23: Design review with PM and Console; acceptance criteria clarified to include backfill and reconciliation thresholds. PM requested a per-route sampling flag to allow high-cardinality customers to limit retained rows.
2026-03-03: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6124) - initial assembler implementation + unit tests. Requesting review from Linnea (observability) and Omar (billing).
2026-03-10: Observability hooks added: pipeline trace ids, tag propagation, and per-job metrics exposed to Grafana dashboard (link below). Running canary job on staging for two days.

2026-03-14: Canary run completed. End-to-end 95p processing time ~3.8 minutes under staging load. Two reconciliation anomalies observed (both caused by duplicate ledgers from a replication bug; incident logged). Next: address deduplication at ingress and add incident learnings to runbook.
implementation_notes: Implementation will use Flink for the assembly job and a lightweight enrichment lambda at producers to attach route/model tags. Outputs will be written to a partitioned Parquet dataset (s3://redwood-analytics/assembled/econ/) partitioned by date and region. Backfill tool will be an idempotent Spark job that writes to the same dataset with row-level dedupe by unique attribution key.
risks_mitigation: Risk: late-arriving events cause attribution drift. Mitigation: sliding reconciliation window (default 48h), backfill utility, and idempotent write semantics. Risk: high-cardinality customers increase storage cost. Mitigation: per-route sampling and retention TTL configurable in Console.
review_feedback: Linnea: please add explicit propagation of request_trace_id through all enrichment steps (accepted).
Omar (billing): require a ledger checksum in assembled rows to speed reconciliation (actioned).
PM (Jules): expose a per-customer anomaly score on Console when reconciliation mismatch > threshold (follow-up ticket created).
